subtype: Approach: writing and rehearsing the speech [Action]
passage: Hafsa, you're nervous about tomorrow's speech, so listen to your Baljeet Uncle. At sixteen I stood for house captain. I wrote my speech on the back of a calendar page. One promise: proper drainage so the ground would not flood during monsoon practice. One story: the day my shoes floated away in the middle of a football match. I read it to the mirror every night. Then I read it to my friend Gulshan, who timed me on his watch: three minutes ten. Too long. I cut every "as we all know" and "respected teachers and friends," and got it down to two minutes flat. On the day, the hall laughed at the shoes and remembered the drainage. I won by a small margin, and Gulshan claimed half the credit.

qa.q: What was the one promise in Baljeet's speech?
qa.a: The promise was proper drainage so the ground would not flood during monsoon practice.

qa.q: How might Baljeet have felt while reading to the mirror each night, and what does it show?
qa.a: Baljeet was probably nervous but determined, shown by the nightly practice and the willingness to be timed and corrected.

qa.q: What choice in the story shortened the speech, and why did it help?
qa.a: Cutting the filler phrases brought it to two minutes, because a shorter speech keeps the one promise and the story clear.

qa.q: How did Gulshan help in the story?
qa.a: Gulshan timed the speech on his watch and showed that it was too long at three minutes ten.

grounding: The candidate drafts a two-minute speech with one clear promise and one story, practises before a mirror and a friend, and trims filler after timing it.
